channel.title: World News
channel.description: Aggregated headlines linking to original publishers

item.title: Iran live updates: Tehran warns US against 'miscalculation,' tanker hit in strait
item.description: President Donald Trump announced "major combat operations" against Iran on Feb. 28.

item.title: Trump Asia trip live updates: Trump greets Putin, Xi as APEC summit begins
item.description: Trump is scheduled this week to participate in the first-ever trilateral meeting with Putin and Xi.

item.title: WATCH: Dog sniffs out baby's medical condition
item.description: ABC News' Danny New talks to a mother in England whose family dog's actions helped alert her that her baby boy had a congenital heart condition.

item.title: Chinese cars shake up Ivory Coast's auto industry
item.description: In the space of just a few years, more than a dozen Chinese carmakers have established themselves in Ivory Coast and are becoming increasingly visible on the country's streets. How have they managed to win over a growing number of customers? FRANCE 24's Jean Barrère and Eunice Stolz-Masson report.

item.title: 'A masterpiece of the gaming industry': GTA 'most expensive' entertainment production in history
item.description: François Picard is pleased to welcome Olivier Mauco, President of the European Video Game Observatory and Lecturer at Paris Dauphine University. For Spotlight, he discusses the extraordinary anticipation surrounding GTA 6, the game's enduring popularity and the economics of blockbuster video game production. “It's kind of the masterpiece of the game industry,” says Mauco of Grand Theft Auto, whose next instalment has generated considerable anticipation following a 13-year hiatus.

item.title: Pineapple pizza debate reignites after Italian chef sacked in Australia
item.description: An Italian chef in Australia has lost his job after refusing to put pineapple on a pizza - calling it "an insult" to his culture. He then took his case to an employment tribunal, but his claim was dismissed. The case has reignited one the debate over what many, particularly in Italy consider to be culinary heresy. Our colleagues from France 2 report on the fallout from Rome.

item.title: Democrat Mary Peltola wins US Senate race in Alaska
item.description: Democrat Mary Peltola ​won Alaska's US Senate race on Tuesday, projections from US media showed, defeating Republican incumbent Dan Sullivan and giving her party its ninth Senate flip of the midterm elections and a commanding 56-44 majority in the upper house of Congress. France 24's Washington correspondent Fraser Jackson has the latest.

item.title: Trump arrives in China ahead of trilateral summit with Putin and Xi
item.description: Donald Trump arrived in Shenzhen, China on Wednesday, ahead of a historic trilateral on the sidelines of the APEC summit with his Russian and Chinese counterparts. The three men are expected to address the wars in Ukraine and Iran as well as nuclear disarmament.

item.title: Woman shot in Glasgow as police hunt attacker
item.description: Police are looking for an attacker after a woman was shot in Glasgow.

item.title: Rubio says 'zero' information that US tech outages are linked
item.description: Secretary of State Marco Rubio on Tuesday sought to assure Americans that there’s "zero" information that a cascade of service outages are related to each other or to a malign actor. Outages that shut down email for many companies and grounded thousands of flights over the past few days extended to the US National Security Agency on Tuesday, disrupting classified communications.

item.title: Israeli parliament elects speaker backed by Netanyahu opponents
item.description: Israel's parliament voted on Tuesday to select a new speaker opposed to the agenda of Benjamin Netanyahu, a potential first step in rolling back the prime minister's divisive political agenda even as his main rival struggles to form a government. France 24's correspondent Noga Tarnopolsky has the details.

item.title: 'Failures, incompetence, broken promises': Deutsche Bank exposed in major leak
item.description: PRESS REVIEW – Wednesday, November 18: A joint investigation following the leak of 15 million documents shows that Deutsche Bank turned a blind eye to the criminal activities of some of its clients. Next, for its 175th birthday, The New York Times has chosen the top 10 stories that made history. Wired is focusing on the moments that defined 2026. Finally, we bring you a story about American parents whose children dream of becoming Formula 1 drivers. But how much does that dream cost?

item.title: Waymo driverless cars barred from California freeways following troubling incidents
item.description: The state of California has slapped a temporary freeway ban on Waymo's autonomous cars

item.title: Russia, China look to deepen ties at APEC as Trump arrives
item.description: China's leader Xi Jinping urged closer political and military ties between his country and Russia, as he met with President Vladimir Putin in Shenzhen on Wednesday on the sidelines of the APEC summit. It comes as Donald Trump arrives in China for trilateral talks with Xi and Putin.

item.title: Greetings from a Berlin square, where an artist's statue watches over children at play
item.description: Children frolic around the ever-watchful and calm Käthe Kollwitz cast in bronze, in a square named after the German artist, whose work often depicted children in the wake of World War I.

item.title: Grand Theft Auto VI is a grounded love story, a gonzo crime thriller and a gaming triumph
item.description: An inspired synthesis of violent satire and contemplative storytelling, Grand Theft Auto VI is more mature and ambitious than any prior game in the record-breaking franchise.

item.title: Turkish pro-opposition broadcaster taken off air after police raid
item.description: Turkish authorities took pro-opposition Sozcu TV off air in a pre-dawn raid on Tuesday and appointed a trustee to run the channel and its website, prosecutors said, extending a crackdown on the opposition and renewing concerns about media freedom.

item.title: US loses measles-free status as cases soar
item.description: The United States lost its hard-fought measles elimination status after 26 years, the Pan American Health Organization said on Tuesday, as the country failed to curb the continuous spread of the highly contagious virus for more than a year. Bolivia and Mexico have also lost their measles elimination status, the Americas arm of the World Health Organization said.

item.title: Banks, flights, email… What’s behind series of US tech outages?
item.description: US Secretary of State Marco insisted Wednesday that authorities have found "zero evidence" that recent outages across tech platforms are related to one another or due to the work of "nefarious actors." It follows multiple disruptions of everything from US air traffic operations to Microsoft email and messaging to banking and mobile pay. France 24’s Philip Turle takes a closer look.

item.title: Evacuations on the rise in eastern Ukraine as fighting intensifies
item.description: Civilian evacuations are stepping up in eastern Ukraine as fighting intensifies in the Donetsk region. According to figures released by Ukrainian authorities, more than 6,300 residents left the region in the first ten days of November. . In neighbouring Kharkiv region, hundreds of evacuees arrive every day in the city Lozova, many of whom have lost everything.

item.title: US hits out at Ukraine's 'deep strikes' against Russia in rift with EU over war tactics
item.description: Top US defence official Elbridge Colby criticised Ukraine's "deep strikes" against Russia Tuesday, as President Volodymyr Zelensky urged Kyiv's backers to send air defences without delay. His comments, delivered at a gathering of Ukraine's allies in Brussels, was flat out rejected by both Germany and the United Kingdom, who hit back at the Americans' suggestion.

item.title: EU proposes new €45 billion Ukraine loan to be repaid by Russia
item.description: European Commission President Ursula von ⁠der Leyen announced on Wednesday a proposed €45 billion loan to Ukraine for 2027 to help cover around two-thirds ​of Kyiv's financing ​needs. The loan will be repaid ⁠through future ⁠war reparations by Russia, von der Leyen added.

item.title: US loses measles-free status amid worst outbreak in 35 years
item.description: The US has lost its measles-free status after 26 years - for failing to prevent the virus spreading for more than a year.

item.title: Mullin faces congressional hearing in the wake of historic nationwide ground stop
item.description: DHS Secretary Markwayne Mullin will be in the hotseat in Congress Wednesday, following last week's air ground stop and several outages of critical online services.

item.title: Nvidia posts blockbuster quarterly results amid leadership crisis
item.description: AI chipmaker Nvidia posted Q3 revenues double those of last year and 20 percent higher than last quarter, while the company board says it has no intention of reinstating disgraced former CEO Jensen Huang. Also in this edition: gaming tourists flock to Miami amid a marketing blitz for the upcoming release of the latest edition in the "Grand Theft Auto" franchise.

item.title: Trump lands in China with key meetings with Xi and Putin on the agenda
item.description: Xi paid Trump a special honor by greeting him on the tarmac after Air Force One arrived in Shenzhen, reciprocating a gesture made by the U.S. president during Xi's visit to Washington in September.

item.title: Congressional Republicans push Howard Lutnick, Jensen Huang to testify about Nvidia
item.description: Senate Banking Committee Chairman Tim Scott, a Republican, sent letters to both Huang and Lutnick to publicly testify in front of the committee

item.title: Trump says ‘taking seriously’ reports Iran planning Washington dirty-bomb attack
item.description: President Donald Trump said on Tuesday the US was taking seriously the possibility that Iran could be planning an attack involving a so-called dirty bomb in Washington, after ‌being asked about a CNN ⁠report citing US intelligence assessments. Iran's Foreign Ministry spokesperson denied the allegations in a post on X on Tuesday, calling them "baseless."

item.title: 'All eyes on talks with Putin, Xi' as Trump arrives at APEC summit
item.description: US President Donald Trump arrived in China on Wednesday where the Asia-Pacific Economic Cooperation (APEC) summit is taking place. However, all eyes will be on a historic trilateral meeting between Trump Chinese President Xi Jinping and Russia's Vladimir Putin on Thursday. Trump has said that the talks would cover the wars in Iran and Ukraine as well as nuclear disarmament.

item.title: How the East Potomac golf course became a D.C. landmark — and what could happen to it
item.description: A federal judge is keeping East Potomac Park open for now, but hasn't ordered the government to keep the municipal golf course operational.

item.title: OpenAI announces new AI safety program; researchers worry it won't be enough
item.description: OpenAI CEO Sam Altman said he would grant "employee level" access to outside researchers to evaluate AI safety. The pilot program appears much more restrictive.

item.title: Iran-backed militias tortured him, but Iraqi environmentalist refuses to quit
item.description: Iran-backed militias kidnapped and tortured him, but Iraqi environmentalist is still on a mission to save marshes, and a way of life stretching back to the dawn of history.

item.title: China and the U.S. are still the biggest polluters, but only China is doing better
item.description: The two largest emitters of greenhouse gases are China and the United States. Now, the countries' stories are diverging: many Chinese provinces are reducing coal use, while the U.S. is falling behind on climate technologies.

item.title: Special education teachers shared their stories. You told NPR you felt seen
item.description: NPR is following along as about a dozen special education teachers navigate this school year and share their joys and challenges. Listeners say they're not alone.

item.title: Poundland owner Gordon Brothers sets deadline for final solvent bids
item.description: Poundland's owner is seeking final bids on Wednesday from companies wanting to buy the discount retailer in a solvent deal that would stave off its collapse into administration.

item.title: Italy approves anti-semitism law despite concerns over freedom of expression
item.description: Italy's ​parliament on Tuesday approved a new bill aimed at combating anti-semitism – which lists some forms of criticism of ⁠Israel as examples of anti-semitic conduct – despite concerns that it could limit freedom of expression and advocacy for Palestinian rights. The law will not impose financial ⁠penalties or criminal sanctions for offenders.

item.title: Democrat defeats Republican in Alaska in final midterms Senate race
item.description: Democrat Mary Peltola has defeated incumbent Republican Dan Sullivan to complete a sweeping victory for the party in the Senate in the US midterm elections.

item.title: AFCON 2027 qualifiers: Senegal and five other nations secure spot
item.description: The first teams to qualify for the 2027 Africa Cup of Nations have been decided. Senegal, Cameroon and Morocco are among them.

item.title: Trump's pick Heidi Overton dropped as nominee for FDA commissioner
item.description: Dr. Heidi Overton’s nomination to lead the Food and Drug Administration was dropped on Tuesday, a White House official confirmed to ABC News.

item.title: Peltola defeats Sullivan in Alaska Senate race, expanding Democratic majority
item.description: Democrat Mary Peltola defeated Republican Sen. Dan Sullivan in Alaska on Tuesday, completing a political comeback in a state that US President Donald Trump has repeatedly won by wide margins. Her victory gives Democrats a 56-44 Senate majority, marking their biggest net gain in Senate seats since 1958.

item.title: Xi Jinping calls for global cooperation on AI and free trade at APEC summit
item.description: Chinese President Xi Jinping called on Wednesday for stronger global cooperation on artificial intelligence and free trade, as he opened the APEC summit in Shenzhen ahead of an expected meeting with US President Donald Trump. Trade tensions and new US chip export restrictions are set to feature prominently.

item.title: NJ sues to compel ICE facility operator to comply with subpoena in medical probe
item.description: The New Jersey AG is suing the operator of an ICE detention center for failing to comply with a subpoena issued in its probe into medical conditions at the facility.

item.title: Mullin defends taking government plane to LSU-Texas game after ground stop
item.description: “Secretary Mullin abides by all ethics requirements," a DHS spokesperson said.

item.title: William and Kate host glittering Earthshot Prize ceremony in Mumbai
item.description: The Prince and Princess of Wales have hosted a star-studded event in Mumbai to celebrate the winners of the Earthshot Prize.

item.title: WATCH: Eagles Autism Foundation staff shine on game day
item.description: ABC News' Will Reeve visits Lincoln Financial Field to meet neurodivergent employees helping make Philadelphia Eagles game days special through the team's commitment to autism inclusion.

item.title: Senate Democrats demand briefings about FAA ground stop amid $50B budget ask
item.description: The funding would go to new air traffic control centers and other improvements.

item.title: WATCH: CMA Awards unveil star-studded presenter lineup for country’s biggest night
item.description: ABC News' Hanna Battah reports the buzziest stories of the day in "GMA" Pop News.

item.title: Police in Philippines pursue three charges against Thomas Markle Sr
item.description: Filipino police are pursuing three charges against Thomas Markle Sr relating to child sexual abuse images, Sky News understands.

item.title: WATCH: National Geographic reveals its pictures of the year
item.description: The magazine's December issue showcases 25 of the most captivating and awe-inspiring images of 2026, selected by its editors.

item.title: Nvidia releases first results since Jensen Huang's resignation
item.description: Nvidia's chairman has reiterated the company does not intend to reinstate Jensen Huang as CEO after he said he would be honoured to return to the role.

item.title: Duffy asked for $50B for air traffic control after ground stop, a marked increase
item.description: The nationwide ground stop thrust funding for the FAA into the spotlight as Transportation Secretary Duffy and President Trump call for more money to fix a broken system.

item.title: The advice Biden got from Mitt Romney, and other takeaways from his memoir
item.description: Biden's memoir "Promise Me, America," which drops Tuesday, recounts his 2020 run for the presidency, his years in the White House and his tumultuous 2024 run.

item.title: Who's performing at Glastonbury 2027?
item.description: Harry Styles, Sam Fender and Billie Eilish have been announced as next year's Glastonbury Festival headliners.

item.title: Prague train crash leaves 46 people injured
item.description: Two trains have collided into each other near the main railway station in Prague, injuring 46 people.

item.title: WATCH: SUV crashes into 2 driverless taxis
item.description: Police in Phoenix are investigating what led to a multi-vehicle crash involving two Waymos as self-driving cars expand into more cities across the U.S.

item.title: WATCH: Fiona the hippo gets a super-sized tummy ache
item.description: The Cincinnati Zoo shared that its most famous resident will be getting monitored around the clock after she "ingested an object that a visitor accidentally tossed into her habitat."

item.title: UK sanctions eight firms building Israeli settlements in the West Bank
item.description: The UK has sanctioned eight firms building Israeli settlements in the West Bank.

item.title: Three Melbourne Cup trophies worth £500k each stolen
item.description: Police are searching for three Melbourne Cup trophies collectively worth more than £1.5m after they were stolen from a display cabinet at a racecourse in Melbourne.

item.title: WATCH: Pope Leo leaves Peru after historic 12-day South America trip
item.description: Pope Leo departed Peru on Monday concluding an emotional 12-day trip to South America as he recovers from cancer surgery. ABC News’ Melissa Adan reports.

item.title: WATCH: NYC teen builds candle business with refillable cement containers
item.description: What started as helping his sister make candles for a birthday party at age 13 has turned into a thriving business for New York City teen Christon Lennon.

item.title: WATCH: Meet the rental car manager going viral for keeping customers calm during ground stop
item.description: Perley Provost, manager of Enterprise Rent-A-Car at Denver International Airport, shares how he kept stranded passengers calm and hydrated during Friday's widespread ground stop.

item.title: WATCH: Trump blames Biden administration for FAA ground stop & other stories
item.description: Nationwide FAA ground stop resulted from equipment failure, says administrator; Anthropic to price its IPO this week; NOAA reports strong El Niño expected to peak in the New Year

item.title: 'Everybody's shell-shocked': GOP operatives face 2028 prospects after midterm defeats
item.description: GOP sources told ABC News the party leaned on culture wars over costs and lost key Latino voters. Some doubt JD Vance is still the presumptive 2028 nominee.

item.title: WATCH: Grammy nominees for Album of the Year, Song of the Year
item.description: Here are the nominees for Album of the Year and Song of the Year at the 2027 Grammys.

item.title: WATCH: Who are the nominees for the 2027 Grammys?
item.description: ABC News' Chris Connelly breaks down the nominees for the 69th Grammy Awards with Raye leading the field with 11 nominations.

item.title: Actor Noel Clarke appears in court over alleged sexual offences
item.description: Actor Noel Clarke has appeared in court after being charged with alleged sexual offences against five women.
